items.title: Morning Briefing: Oct. 24, 2026
items.excerpt: Here's a rundown of all the news you need to start Saturday, including Jordan declaring three days of mourning after a deadly church attack that killed at least seven people, a US-brokered temporary ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky, and a Russia-Ukraine prisoner swap of 270 servicemen. ## TOP STORIES ... Jordan declared three days of national mourning for the victims of a "terrorist attack" on a Greek Orthodox church in a village in the southern Karak governorate, after gunmen opened fire at a funeral, killing at least seven people and injuring 28, according to officials. King Abdullah said the attack will be met with the "harshest retaliation," and that “those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity.” Public Security Directorate spokesman Amer Sartawi described the shooting as a "criminal incident" and said security forces are pursuing the perpetrators. - US first lady announces Oleshky ceasefire between Russia, Ukraine US first lady Melania Trump announced an agreement between Russia and Ukraine to establish a temporary ceasefire in the southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky, intended to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and the evacuation of civilians who wish to leave, with the White House saying the truce is scheduled to begin on Oct. 29. "The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster," she said, adding that the city's remaining population is primarily elderly residents in urgent need of medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water. President Donald Trump said his wife’s focus is "to save children" and that "both sides are cooperating with her.” ... Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said military officials are working to coordinate the ceasefire and that "those who wish to leave the town will be able to do so," adding that the operation requires extensive and complex preparations and that the evacuation is expected to take at least several days. - Russia, Ukraine swap 270 servicemen each in latest prisoner exchange Russian said Moscow and Kyiv swapped 270 servicemen each in the latest prisoner exchange between the two countries, with the returned Russian servicemen currently in neighboring Belarus. The Defense Ministry added that the service members will return to Russia after receiving necessary psychological and medical assistance and will be transported to medical facilities for further treatment and rehabilitation. ... ## NEWS IN BRIEF - Israeli forces shot and killed two Palestinians in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron following allegations they opened fire at Israeli settlers, wounding five people. - Australia imposed sanctions on two North Korean companies and two financial brokers for their alleged role in funding Pyongyang’s nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs through fraudulent IT employment schemes. - Storm Austen left more than 160,000 households without power in France, as strong winds prompted weather alerts in 23 departments in the northwest. - A cybersecurity incident disrupted online systems in public schools in Richmond, capital of the US state of Virginia, forcing schools to shift to a technology-free learning environment while remaining open. - President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said Türkiye continues efforts to promote peace across regions, highlighting Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchanges and mediation initiatives in Africa. - The Collective Security Treaty Organization may decide on Armenia’s membership status at its summit in Moscow next month, with Secretary General Taalatbek Masadykov saying the country’s withdrawal "could happen" if the issue is raised. - Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Ottawa is seeking Türkiye’s expertise to strengthen its defenses and build joint military capabilities, while rejecting US allegations of Canadian election interference and reaffirming that Canada will never become America’s 51st state. - International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol warned that the global energy crisis could persist into 2027, saying he sees little reason to expect a return to normal next year. - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the "immediate closure" of Hebron and instructed security forces to prepare a "full lockdown" of the occupied West Bank. - Greece’s parliament passed legislation banning children younger than 15 from accessing major social media platforms, with the measure set to take effect on Jan. 1. - Austria expelled four Russian diplomats for activities deemed incompatible with their diplomatic status, with the Foreign Ministry citing findings by security authorities but providing no details. - The Kremlin said the first tanker carrying Russian diesel fuel under a deal with the US has departed for its buyers, with additional shipments expected to continue regularly. - Russia said trilateral peace talks on Ukraine are scheduled for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, with discussions set to focus on security guarantees for Russia and Ukraine after a peace deal. - France will deploy 70,000 police officers and gendarmes ahead of nationwide protests, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez vowing an "extremely firm" response to violence, looting, and attacks on public buildings. - Ebola has spread to an eighth province in the Democratic Republic of Congo, as the UN food agency warns that hunger threatens treatment continuity for patients and 3.5 million people in outbreak-affected areas face crisis-level food insecurity. - The Pentagon released its seventh batch of UFO records, including reports of a fast-moving black triangular object spotted by federal agents near a secure US facility, historical sightings, and documents on alleged paranormal activity. - Canadian high diver Molly Carlson became the first woman to dive from a free-floating iceberg, completing a nearly 15-meter (49-foot) backward dive into freezing North Atlantic waters off Newfoundland and Labrador. - A new Israeli poll showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc losing three seats to 48, trailing the opposition bloc’s projected 54 seats ahead of the Oct. 27 election, with neither side projected to secure a governing majority. - Gold prices fell toward a three-month low as a selloff in technology stocks prompted investors to cover losses elsewhere, while rising oil prices fueled inflation concerns and expectations of higher interest rates. - Greece suspended state funding to its basketball federation and ordered financial audits amid a match-fixing and bribery investigation involving federation President Vangelis Liolios and five others facing judicial proceedings. - Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan warned that a new military attack on Iran would widen regional conflict, saying military intervention was “by no means a solution” amid concerns about renewed US-Israeli strikes. - Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was hospitalized after collapsing while watching the club’s reserve team train, with the 40-year-old Belgian set to undergo medical examinations as his coaching staff takes charge until further notice. - Yemen said it neutralized 620 Houthi fighters and destroyed or damaged 190 military vehicles and weapons systems in 1,392 operations under "Operation Dawn of Yemen" in 24 hours. - US President Donald Trump warned of possible renewed military action against Iran if Tehran rejects negotiations, while saying Washington would "take care of Cuba" after dealing with Iran. - The International Atomic Energy Agency said it is ready to verify Iran’s nuclear activities, with chief Rafael Grossi urging a diplomatic agreement and saying most technical preparations needed for adequate verification have been completed. - The Trump administration removed several Canadian products from its 50% tariff list, with changes taking effect Oct. 30 ahead of hard-fought US midterm elections.

items.excerpt: More than 400,000 protest across France, challenging Macron as Paris clashes erupt PARIS (AP) — Clashes erupted in Paris as a mass march drew to a close Saturday. More than 400,000 people rallied across France over school funding and soaring living costs, challenging President Emmanuel Macron. Police made nearly 1,000 arrests. The Paris march began peacefully but turned violent near its endpoint. Masked protesters hurled objects and fireworks at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons. The Interior Ministry reported 410,000 protesters nationwide, while the CGT union estimated nearly 800,000. This unrest is testing Macron's authority in the final months of his presidency before elections in May. Ukraine and Russia eye new peace talks — and Melania Trump's mission — but steep obstacles remain KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukraine and Russia have signaled willingness to resume peace talks and back a humanitarian mission led by U.S. First lady Melania Trump, but deep disagreements over territory and security guarantees underscore obstacles to ending the war. U.S. President Donald Trump is pushing for a new round of negotiations, potentially in mid-November, as Russia continues to demand control of Ukrainian regions it illegally annexed but does not fully control. Kyiv rejects any suggestion of unilateral withdrawal and says stronger Western pressure on Moscow is needed to advance peace efforts.

items.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — Americans largely shrugged off higher prices last month and stepped up their spending at retail stores and online, providing a boost to the economy. Retail sales rose a seasonally adjusted 1.7% in October from September, the U.S. Commerce Department said Tuesday. That’s the biggest gain since March and up from 0.8% in the previous month. Much of the sales increase also reflected higher prices. ... Tuesday’s retail sales figures aren’t adjusted for inflation, which rose 0.9% in October, the government said last Wednesday. In some categories, such as gas station sales, which rose 3.9% in October, a jump in gas prices accounted for nearly all the gain. Gas prices rose 3.7% in October, according to the government’s inflation report. ... Yet inflation has eroded those gains for most Americans. Prices jumped 6.2% in October from a year earlier, the government said last Wednesday — the most in 31 years.

items.excerpt: Los Angeles (AP) — Local election officials across California are confused and frustrated after receiving letters from President Donald Trump’s Justice Department demanding that county registrars sequester ballots that the federal government believes were sent to noncitizen voters ahead of the midterm elections. The letters, which were sent on Friday, ask for sensitive information, including Social Security numbers, on roughly 20,000 voters. It is illegal for noncitizens to register to vote or cast a ballot. The administration has insisted that immigrants voting is a major problem nationwide, when in fact it is quite rare, as even its own investigations have shown.

items.title: Box Office: 'Clayface' Takes No. 1, 'You Can See Everything' Follows
items.excerpt: Box Office: 'Clayface' Takes No. 1, 'You Can See Everything' Follows Oct 24, 2026 8:44am PT ... # Box Office: ‘Clayface’ Lands at No. 1 with $10.4 Million Debut, ‘You Can See Everything’ Adds $6.14 Million on Friday By Payton Turkeltaub ... Clayface might have been a considerably nicher choice for a feature film than DC’s “Supergirl” and “Superman,” but that didn’t stop audiences from showing out to catch the Batman supervillain’s gory, nightmare-inducing origin story at the box office this weekend. ... The new release generated $10.4 million from 3,458 North American theaters on Friday, taking the No. 1 spot. It’s a strong start for the film, which looks to pull in $24 million by Sunday. ... Directed by James Watkins, “Clayface” follows the titular Batman villain, a rising movie star also known as Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries), who volunteers for a highly experimental medical procedure after his face is severely disfigured. Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan also star. Variety’s Guy Lodge called the film “its own ugly animal; perhaps the characters and conflicts introduced here would pall if given the franchise treatment, but in the context of a single, genre-melding romp, they’re fresh and ickily enjoyable.” ... A24’s much-hyped Elizabeth Holmes documentary “ You Can See Everything” landed in second place on Friday, making $6.14 million from 2,655 North American theaters, up from 855 at opening weekend. The buzzy doc has made $31.7 million domestically so far. Rival estimates suggest the film will gross another $20 million by Sunday. ... Comedian Nathan Fielder and “Primetime” filmmaker Lance Oppenheim quietly worked on the movie for more than three years, which offers an unhinged look at the Theranos founder a month before she began an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. In addition to being eligible for best documentary feature at the 99th Academy Awards, the film will also be submitted across the board as seen on A24’s awards site: best picture, director, production design, cinematography, costume design, film editing, makeup and hairstyling, sound and original score. Laika’s “ Wildwood,” another new release, landed in third place on Friday, grossing $4.28 million from 2,942 North American theaters. Featuring a voice cast that includes Carey Mulligan, Jacob Tremblay and others, the stop-motion film looks to bring in $11.2 million by Sunday. Directed by Travis Knight, “Wildwood” revolves around a teenage girl who travels with a classmate into an enchanted forest after her brother is abducted. Strong reviews should continue to propel the lavish film at the box office, which carries a substantial $100 million price tag. Black Bear’s “ Wicker” followed in fourth place, earning $2.36 million on Friday from 1,471 North American theaters. The offbeat romantic comedy, directed by Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer, is targeting a $5.5 million opening weekend. Described as an “audacious comedic fable,” “Wicker” tells the love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) who commissions a husband from the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). Alexander Skarsgård plays said husband. Elizabeth Debicki also stars. ... Coming in fifth was Legendary Entertainment’s “Street Fighter.” The action film grossed $2.34 million on Friday and should add another $8.4 million by Sunday, bringing its cumulative gross to $46.7 million. “Street Fighter,” directed by Kitao Sakurai, stars Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji as two estranged fighters in the 90s who are recruited to enter a tournament that forces them to face off against each other.

items.title: New Shotgun 10/24/26 - Everything Action
items.excerpt: Timo Tjahjanto directing The Burnout action comedy: With The Beekeeper 2 coming up early next year, Timo Tjahjanto has found his next project, an action comedy called The Burnout. The movie follow a washed up CIA agent who is living as a burnout in Ibiza when he’s pulled back into action. Afterlife with Archie finds director: The upcoming Disney+ series Afterlife with Archie has found a director in Alfonso Gomez-Rejon, who will direct the first two episodes and serve as an executive producer alongside Greg Berlanti. He previously worked on Hunters and directed Me and Earl and the Dying Girl. The series is based on the Archie comic by Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa and Francesco Francavilla, where Riverdale becomes the location of a zombie outbreak after a spell by Sabrina the Teenage Witch goes wrong. items.excerpt: Following his historic, sold-out three-night run at Yankee Stadium, JAŸ-Z and Roc Nation have announced second stadium shows in London and Los Angeles due to unprecedented fan demand, expanding one of the year's most highly anticipated series of global performances. The Yankee Stadium run shattered the venue's all-time concert attendance records across all three nights and made JAŸ-Z the first artist ever to sell out three consecutive shows at the venue. A second Los Angeles show has also been added for Saturday, October 24, 2026 at SoFi Stadium, following the previously announced October 23 performance. These must-see performances celebrate JAŸ-Z's remarkable 30-year career and iconic catalog that has shaped music and culture around the world. Tickets for the new dates will be available starting Wednesday, July 29 at 10am local time via presales. In Los Angeles, Citi is the official card of the JAŸ-Z 30 performances. Citi cardmembers will have access to presale tickets beginning Wednesday, July 29 at 10am local time until 10pm local time through the Citi Entertainment program. For complete presale details visit www.citientertainment.com. The general on-sale for the new dates will begin Thursday, July 30 at 10am local time at livenation.com.
